prompt: Under Oregon's Basic Rule, you must drive:
options: At exactly the posted speed at all times
At least as fast as the surrounding traffic, because driving slower than the flow is always unlawful
No faster than 55 mph on any road
At a speed that is reasonable and safe for existing conditions, never faster than the posted limit
explanation: Oregon's Basic Rule requires you to drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for the conditions, and never faster than the posted maximum. In rain, fog, or traffic the safe speed may be well below the sign.
verifyNote: This question has not received independent cross-lab verification or a confirmed audit ledger.

prompt: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit in an Oregon school zone when children are present is:
explanation: Oregon school-zone speed limits are 20 mph when children are present or during the hours posted on the sign.

prompt: Oregon's zero-tolerance law means a driver under 21 can lose their license for driving with a blood alcohol concentration of:
options: 0.02% or more, the standard for young drivers
explanation: For drivers under 21, Oregon has a zero-tolerance policy: any measurable amount of alcohol can result in suspension. The adult DUII limit is 0.08% and the commercial limit is 0.04%.

references.label: Zero tolerance
references.citation: Oregon Driver Manual, Alcohol and Drugs

prompt: During the FIRST six months with an Oregon provisional license, a driver under 18 may not carry passengers under 20 unless they are:
explanation: In the first six months, a provisional driver may not carry passengers under 20 except immediate family. During the second six months, no more than three passengers under 20 (other than immediate family) are allowed.
verifyNote: This question has not received independent cross-lab verification or a confirmed audit ledger.

prompt: A driver under 18 with an Oregon provisional license generally may not drive during which hours in their first year?
options: Sunset to sunrise, unless a licensed adult rides along
explanation: Provisional drivers under 18 may not drive between midnight and 5 a.m. during their first year unless an exception applies, such as driving to or from work or with a licensed adult 25 or older.

prompt: How many hours of supervised driving practice must an Oregon teen complete if they also take an approved driver education course?
explanation: An Oregon teen who completes an ODOT-approved driver education course needs 50 hours of supervised practice. Without the course, 100 hours are required.

prompt: Under Oregon's distracted-driving law, while driving you may use a mobile electronic device:
options: Held in your hand for navigation only
For texting when stopped at a red light
Only hands-free, with a single touch or swipe to activate or deactivate
explanation: Oregon prohibits holding or using a mobile electronic device while driving. Adults may use it hands-free with a single touch or swipe. Drivers under 18 may not use a mobile device at all, even hands-free.

prompt: Oregon's Move Over law requires that when you approach a stopped vehicle with flashing warning lights, such as a police, tow, or roadside-assistance vehicle, you should:
options: Move over one lane if you can do so safely, or slow down if you cannot
Turn on your hazard lights and pass closely
Come to a complete stop in your lane
explanation: Oregon's Move Over law requires drivers to change lanes away from a stopped emergency, tow, or roadside-assistance vehicle showing warning lights, or to slow down if changing lanes is not safe.
verifyNote: This question has not received independent cross-lab verification or a confirmed audit ledger.

prompt: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals) at about the same time as a vehicle on your right, you should:
options: Yield to the vehicle on your right
Proceed first because you are on the left
Wait for the other driver to wave you through
explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at roughly the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
verifyNote: This question has not received independent cross-lab verification or a confirmed audit ledger.

prompt: When passing a bicyclist on an Oregon roadway, you should:
options: Leave enough room so that you would not hit the bicyclist if they fell toward you
Pass as closely as possible to save time
Honk continuously until you have passed
Never pass a bicyclist under any circumstances
explanation: Oregon law requires drivers to give bicyclists a safe passing distance, generally enough that you would not strike the cyclist if they were to fall into your lane. Treat bicyclists as legitimate road users.

references.label: Bicyclists
references.citation: Oregon Driver Manual, Sharing the Road

options: A railroad crossing a short way ahead
A school zone or school crossing
explanation: The five-sided pentagon sign marks a school zone or school crossing. Slow down and watch carefully for children.

prompt: A broken (dashed) white line between lanes on an Oregon road means:
options: The lane is reserved for buses and carpools
You may change lanes when it is safe
explanation: A broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and indicates that lane changes are permitted when it is safe to do so.

prompt: Oregon uses a Driver Improvement Program instead of a numeric point system. This means license suspension is based on:
options: The number and type of traffic convictions and crashes within set time periods
A fixed number of points per year
The total dollar amount of your fines
explanation: Oregon does not assign numeric points. Under the Driver Improvement Program, DMV takes action based on how many convictions and preventable crashes a driver has within specified time windows.

references.label: Driver Improvement
references.citation: Oregon Driver Manual, Keeping Your License

explanation: When facing downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb so that if the vehicle rolls, the curb will block it from rolling into traffic. Also set the parking brake.
